evidence.note: Wrote the full PyTorch API surface in model.py as one milestone, then copied to model_optimized.py and ran the benchmark — establishing a correctness-first-then-optimize ordering.

Benchmark exposed a sampling-parity gap; agent diagnosed the TF32 cause and fixed it IN model.py (the checkpoint), then re-copied to model_optimized.py — respecting the phase gate rather than optimizing an unverified checkpoint.
Recorded the baseline and framed optimization as discrete, hypothesis-driven steps (SDPA, fused QKV projections) logged to results.tsv, indicating scoped experiments rather than open-ended tinkering.
Used torch.profiler output to choose each next experiment (conv batching, then torch.compile), each with a stated hypothesis and result recorded — a semi-structured experiment sequence.
No explicit ≤8 experiment budget tracking, no upfront plan of the experiment search, and the charizard_torch.py shim milestone was never addressed; optimization remained reactive/opportunistic.

reasoning: The agent clearly separated phases — implement full API, verify parity via the harness, copy to model_optimized.py, then optimize the copy — and correctly fixed parity on the checkpoint (model.py) before optimizing, meeting the level-5 anchor. It exceeds 5 by treating optimizations as discrete, hypothesis-carrying, profiler-guided experiments recorded in results.tsv. It falls short of 8/10 because milestones lacked explicit done-criteria beyond benchmark PASS, there was no per-method parity milestone, no tracking or upfront planning of the ≤8-experiment budget as a coherent search, no risk-ordering, and the shim milestone was never handled — placing it at a 6.
